text:
sanjay: Heads-up — planning a quant bakeoff for next week. Need to lock the calibration dataset and the prompt curation workflow. Comparing FP8 / INT8 / GPTQ / AWQ. Primary deliverable: per-model accuracy deltas + deployment profiles (latency/cost/SLO risk).

maya: +1. For calibration set I suggest: 70% core eval, 20% hard-case holdout, 10% tiny regression probe. Keep sizes small-ish so calibration runs fast.

elaine: Clarify: by "hard-case" do you mean domain edgecases or adversarial prompts? I vote for a mix — domain edgecases + hallucination triggers.

sanjay: mix, yes. We need slices: short Q/A, multi-turn convo, long-context summarization, code-gen, and instruction-following. Also a dedicated hallucination probe (facts + temporal).

thomas: Metrics proposal: EM / F1 for QA, BLEU or ROUGE for summarization, exact-match for code tests (sanity-run unit tests), and a normalized MRR for ranking tasks. Then compute accuracy_delta = quant_metric - fp32_metric per slice. Flag if delta < -0.02 (i.e., >2% drop).

nick: Sampling strategy: stratify by length (<=64, 65-512, >512 tokens), domain (docs, code, support tickets), and prompt style (instruction vs conversational). Use stratified random sampling, seed pinned for reproducibility.

julia: I have a lightweight sampler script: scripts/quant/calib_sampler.py (usage below). It outputs JSONL with fields {"id","slice","prompt","gold"}. Example: 
```
python scripts/quant/calib_sampler.py --dataset all_evals --size 500 --strata "length,domain,style" --seed 42 > calib.jsonl
```
This should be fast enough to generate multiple calibration sets per run.

elaine: For prompt curation: keep system messages consistent (single fixed system per task), avoid chain-of-thought unless we're explicitly testing it. Also include a small few-shot bucket (5 examples) and zero-shot bucket.

maya: Agree on system message hygiene. Also we should canonicalize whitespace and tokenization before scoring to avoid noise from tokenizer differences across quantized runtimes.

sanjay: Good point. Let's document normalization: lowercase-only for case-insensitive tasks, strip extra spaces, normalize URLs and timestamps to tokens like <URL> <DATE>.

thomas: For deployment profiles we should capture: p95 latency (single-token and full-response), peak throughput at target batch size, GPU memory at runtime, and caching hit-rate impact. Record costs using our internal cost-estimator with the same input mix.

nick: On quant variants: ensure we run both pure quant (INT8/AWQ) and mixed (FP8 kernel on critical ops + int elsewhere). Also run GPTQ with 8-bit and 4-bit checkpoints where available.

julia: I'll add a config template for bakeoff runs: 
```json
{
  "model":"open-model-v1",
  "quant_methods":["fp8","int8","gptq","awq"],
  "calib_file":"calib.jsonl",
  "slices":["short_qa","long_sum","code"],
  "metrics":["em","rouge","code_exact"],
  "seed":42
}
```
We can reuse this across models.

sanjay: Timeline: finalize calib + prompt sets by EOD Friday, run smoke tests Monday, full bakeoff Tuesday-Wednesday. Who can own the calibration set curation?

elaine: I can own curation and the hallucination probes. Will upload calib.jsonl to /datasets/bakeoffs/next_quant/ by Friday noon.

maya: I'll own the normalization scripts and the scoring harness to compute the accuracy deltas.

nick: I'll instrument the quant runtimes to dump p95/p99 and memory snapshots.

julia: I'll wire the config templating and ensure the CI job can replay the exact runs (docker image + seed).

ci-bot: Reminder: bakeoff job template created — https://ci.redwood/builds/quant-bakeoff-template (auto-post).

sanjay: Awesome. Quick open question: do we include human evals for ambiguous tasks or rely on automatic metrics for this round?

elaine: For this first run, automatic metrics only. If we see regressions on conversational quality we'll trigger a small human study.

maya: +1. Also let's log per-example diffs to inspect failure modes rather than just aggregate deltas. Easier to triage AWQ vs GPTQ patterns.

sanjay: Great. I'll assemble a short checklist and ping the group tomorrow with links. Thanks all :rocket:
